--- workspace/fetch.sh	
+++ workspace/fetch.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
+
+API="https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/accelerators_accelerateurs-aws"
+
+fetch() {
+    local url="$1"
+    local outfile="$2"
+    local status
+    status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    if [ "$status" -ge 400 ]; then
+        echo "Retrying $url after 5s..."
+        sleep 5
+        status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    fi
+    echo "$status" > "${outfile}.status"
+}
+
+fetch "$API" /workspace/repo.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/" /workspace/root_contents.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md" /workspace/contributing.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/workflows" /workspace/workflows.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yml" /workspace/dependabot_yml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yaml" /workspace/dependabot_yaml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/renovate.json" /workspace/renovate.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.renovaterc.json" /workspace/renovaterc.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/commits" /workspace/commits.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/issues?state=open" /workspace/issues.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/actions/runs" /workspace/actions_runs.json

GC Accelerators (AWS)

AWS has developed a project called the AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA) with the goal to accelerate the GC’s Amazon Web Services (AWS) deployments. It can be found at: https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secure-environment-accelerator and it has been open-sourced by AWS under the Apache-2.0 License.

The ASEA is a tool designed to help deploy and operate secure multi-account, multi-region AWS environments on an ongoing basis and it enables the GC’s Cloud First direction and support for the GC Digital Standards. Using automation, the ASEA reduces the amount of effort required to meet the 12 GC Cloud Guardrails to less than 3 days and also meets many of the Protected B, Medium Integrity, Medium Availability (PBMM) compliance requirements.

The users of this project will be Government of Canada employees deploying cloud-based workloads.

Accélérateurs GC (AWS)

AWS a développé un projet appelé AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA) dans le but d'accélérer les déploiements Amazon Web Services (AWS) du GC. Il peut être trouvé à l’adresse suivante: https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secure-environment-accelerator et il a été open-sourcé par AWS sous la licence Apache-2.0.

L’ASEA est un outil conçu pour aider à déployer et à gérer des environnements AWS sécurisés multi-comptes et multi-régions sur une base continue. Il permet d’orienter vers la direction du GC par l’informatique en nuage d’abord et de prendre en charge les normes numériques du GC. Grâce à l'automatisation, l'ASEA réduit à moins de 3 jours le montant d'effort requis pour répondre aux 12 mesures de sécurité en nuage du GC et répond également à un grand nombre des exigences de conformité Protégé B, intégrité moyenne et disponibilité moyenne (PBMM).

Les utilisateurs de ce projet seront des employés du gouvernement du Canada qui déploieront des charges de travail en nuage.

Comment contribuer

In order to move towards a more flexible design system, the plan is to “decouple” the detailed specs of the templates and patterns from the official "policy documents" - the Canada.ca Specifications and Canada.ca Content Style Guide.
The vision would then be to gradually improve each pattern and template and make into usable code (rather than pictures) with instructions. We could also have a separate library of "experimental patterns and templates", that we could open up to the whole community. We would need to eventually develop a process involving the community for a pattern to go from “experimental” to "approved".

data.text:
The GitHub UI pages are coming back but with a lot of "Uh oh!" and "Sorry, something went wrong" loading errors, likely because heavy JS or because we are being rate limited or require authentication for some parts. However we can still extract useful data from the HTML snippets. The API is rate limited (403).

We need to gather all fields, mostly using HTML pages where possible. Let's systematically fetch the needed pages via `webfetch` and parse what we can.

We have already fetched:
- https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system (repo home page) => gives some metadata (languages, issues 23, pull requests 8, stars 38, forks 17, there are files like README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, etc.)
- https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/tree/master/.github => shows .github contents: workflows directory, dependabot.yml
- https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/tree/master/.github/workflows => shows workflow files: cleanup-previews.yml, jekyll.yml, pr-preview.yml
- https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/actions => shows workflows list including "Cleanup Stale PR Previews", "Copilot", "Dependabot Updates", "Deploy Jekyll site to Pages", "Deploy PR Preview", "pages-build-deployment". Also shows "1,206 workflow runs". So actions exist.

We need to inspect workflow YAML files for security scanners and test steps. Also need to know open issues count, commits (last commit date), license, readme existence, contributing guide, etc.

We can fetch raw files via raw.githubusercontent.com for workflow files and README and LICENSE, etc.

Let's fetch raw files:
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/.github/workflows/jekyll.yml
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/.github/workflows/cleanup-previews.yml
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/.github/workflows/pr-preview.yml
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/README.md
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/LICENSE (or LICENSE.md, etc.)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/design-system/master/.github/dependabot.yml

Also need to get commits and open issues. We can try the API again with a sleep? Maybe use `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/design-system/commits?per_page=1` and see if rate limit resets. But if not, we can try the HTML commits page (maybe with a different URL, e.g., https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/commits/master). The previous fetch returned 429. Maybe we can use `https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/commits` without specifying branch? Let's try later.

Also open issues: `https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/issues` might show a count. Or use API with `?state=open&per_page=1` and look at `Link` header? But we might not have API access. However the repo page shows "Issues 23". That's a count. But we need to filter out PRs. On GitHub, the issues tab count includes PRs in the API? Actually the UI shows "Issues 23". Could be the count of issues and PRs combined? The UI says "Issues 23". Usually that tab shows only issues; the PR count is separate. So the UI "Issues 23" is likely open issues count. But the task says to use API `/repos/canada-ca/design-system/issues?state=open&per_page=100` and filter out PRs. Since API is rate limited, we might have to use the UI number. But if we can't be sure, we might write Unknown.

Let's see what else we can get.

We need `primary_language`. The repo home page shows "Languages: HTML 73.4%, Sass 10.7%, JavaScript 8.3%, CSS 7.3%, Ruby 0.3%". The primary language is likely `HTML`. The API `language` field is usually the most used language. So we can set `primary_language` to `HTML`.

`readme_exists`: The root page shows `README.md` in the file list. So `Yes`.

`licence`: We need to check `license.spdx_id` from API. Since API is rate limited, we can't get it. We need to check for a LICENSE file. The root file list did not show a LICENSE file. It showed README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, Gemfile, etc. No LICENSE. So `licence` = `Unknown`.

`contributing_guide`: The root file list shows `CONTRIBUTING.md`. So `Yes`.

`has_security_scanning_in_ci`: We need to inspect workflow files. Let's fetch them.

`has_tests_in_ci`: Inspect workflow files.

`dependency_update_policy`: We saw `.github/dependabot.yml`. So `Automated`.

`last_commit_date`: Need to get from API or commits page. We can try the HTML commits page with `https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/commits` (maybe without branch). Let's try. Also we can try `https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/commits/master` again with a different user-agent? `webfetch` might be getting blocked. Let's try `curl` via bash with `-L` and maybe `-H "User-Agent: ..."`. The `webfetch` tool is essentially fetching. We can use `bash` with `curl` to fetch raw pages and then parse. But we can also use `webfetch` again.

Let's try using `bash` with `curl` to fetch the commits page and issues page. Since we need to be careful with rate limits, but we can do it.

We also need to count open issues. The UI shows 23. We need to be sure. Could try to fetch the issues API using a different IP? Not possible.

But maybe we can fetch `https://github.com/canada-ca/design-system/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen` to see the list count. The UI might show a count in the tab or on the page.

Let's proceed with fetching raw files and commits page via `bash curl`.

# This workflow uses actions that are not certified by GitHub.

# documentation.

# Sample workflow for building and deploying a Jekyll site to GitHub Pages
name: Deploy Jekyll site to Pages

on:
  # Runs on pushes targeting the default branch
  push:
    branches: ["master"]

  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

# Sets permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN to allow pushing to gh-pages
permissions:
  contents: write

# Allow only one concurrent deployment, skipping runs queued between the run in-progress and latest queued.
# However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.
concurrency:
  group: "production-deploy"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build_and_deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2.3'
          bundler-cache: true
          cache-version: 0

      - name: Build with Jekyll
        run: bundle exec jekyll build
        env:
          JEKYLL_ENV: production

      - name: Deploy to gh-pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./_site
          # keep_files is intentionally set to true so that existing content (including PR preview directories)
          # is not deleted on each deploy. Old preview directories are periodically cleaned up by
          # .github/workflows/cleanup-previews.yml to prevent unbounded growth of the gh-pages branch.
          keep_files: true
          publish_branch: gh-pages

# Contributing

([Français](#comment-contribuer))

## How to Contribute

When contributing, post comments and discuss changes you wish to make via Issues.

Feel free to propose changes by creating Pull Requests. If you don't have write access, editing a file will create a Fork of this project for you to save your proposed changes to. Submitting a change to a file will write it to a new Branch in your Fork, so you can send a Pull Request.

If this is your first time contributing on GitHub, don't worry! Let us know if you have any questions.

### Security

**Do not post any security issues on the public repository!** See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

# Canada.ca design library - evidence-based patterns & templates

In order to move towards a more flexible design system, the plan is to “decouple” the detailed specs of the templates and patterns from the official "policy documents" - the [Canada.ca Specifications](https://design.canada.ca/architecture/canada-content-information-architecture-specification.html) and [Canada.ca Content Style Guide](https://design.canada.ca/style-guide/).

The vision would then be to gradually improve each pattern and template and make into usable code (rather than pictures) with instructions. We could also have a separate library of "experimental patterns and templates", that we could open up to the whole community. We would need to eventually develop a process involving the community for a pattern to go from “experimental” to "approved".
